docs.title: Tiko <--> Hareth
docs.text:
• TIko says that Hareth reminds him of a wolverine.
  • Tiko and Scrap have a friendly competition of seeing who is the fastest climber.

docs.title: Tiko <--> Scrap
docs.text:
• Scrap confided the following in Tiko: Scrap's builder and former master treated Scrap very poorly -- both as a tool and as a person. Very abusive with a god complex. Would physically abuse Scrap for fun. He didn't recognize Scrap as a conscious, feeling being.
  • Tiko told Scrap that Tiko's true form is halfling, but he hates being short so he's always wild shaped as a Simiah. It's a secret between them.

docs.title: Scrap <--> Hareth
docs.text:
• Hareth taught scrap about human emotions to help Scrap better understand non-construct sentient nature:
    • Human emotions / relationships are ebb and flow. Although you may feel disconnected to someone, you will always have that connection with every being you encounter.
  • Scrap has asked Hareth to watch out for Faint Divinities who sow discord. Scrap is worried that, as a Clank, he's not in-tune enough with other non-construct emotions, so he might not recognize when a Faint Divinity is sowing discord.

docs.title: Appearance / Layout
docs.text:
Tree Spire is, like its name implies, a city built onto the trunk and branches of a massive tree. It's main thoroughfare is a winding vine that has been shaped and flattened, twisting around the trunk of the tree. Smaller roads reach out onto the branches. A series of lifts run vertically between branches and down to the ground.

The main part of the city is located in the branches of the tree. Druidic magic forms platforms off the branches where houses and businesses hang in the air. The trunk of the tree itself has been magically hollowed, providing more space for the city. At the top of the tree lies the council chambers and just below that the druid circle where budding druids are trained.

A portion of the tree’s massive roots rise out of the ground twist amongst themselves forming a ring wall around the perimeter of the tree. Much of the ground of this ring is made up of farm land with crisscrossing irrigation channels and rather beautiful bridges.

In contrast to the general beauty of most of the city, a sliver of the ring is taken up by a haphazard town. This town lies in the southern part of the ring and pushes against the bounds of the wall and farmlands. This is also where the only remaining gate to the city lies - the rest being sealed at the onset of the Witherwild. The buildings closest to the tree are relatively nice wood buildings, but the closer they get to the wall, the more hastily built they appear. Many rising several stories containing multiple families.

docs.title: Politics
docs.text:
Tree Spire is led by a trio of Archdruids, the oldest and wisest of whom is Korran. However the more day to day management of the city is led by a council of leaders from various levels of the branches. Tree Spire has long been a sanctuary for those from smaller villages that fell to beasts, disease or some other effect of the Witherwild. However, this is starting to cause a strain on the infrastructure of the city. There are some who speak of closing the city’s gates, but the Archdruids have held firm on their open door stance.

Tree Spire has a tenuous relationship with Haven. Historically, the cities have traded and had amicable relations. However, after Haven’s invasion of Fanewick to harvest every lady’s veil they could find and the subsequent theft of the Reaping Eye, Tree Spire has seen Haven as a threat to the natural order. Trade still occurs between the cities and Korran continues to work out some official deals with Haven, but for the most part these two cities are estranged.

docs.title: Clank-drawn Rendition
docs.text: Note: There are no buildings outside the walls. The Clank hired did not understand my directions.

docs.title: The Haven Arcanum
docs.text:
The Haven Arcanum serves multiple purposes. It's primarily an organization of wizards and sorcerers that serve the interests of Haven. It's supported by a martial arm known as Warders who protect wizards and the Arcanum grounds. The Arcanum is led by five Archmages, the most prominent of whom is Archmage Phylax.

The Arcanum also hosts an academy for training wizards, training grounds for the Warders, and a library said to hold the largest collection of magical tomes, scrolls and artifacts. Public access is permitted to certain areas of the library, but it is highly guarded -- including magical wards.

docs.title: Arcanum layout
docs.text:
• Central spire is home to meeting rooms, the library, offices, and labs
  • Outer spires house Arcanum members
  • Ring of greenery, paths
  • Floating above the ring of greenery are the Archmage towers
  • On the eastern half of the grounds are less impressive buildings and towers that hold classrooms, student housing, kitchens, etc. There are nice paths and greenery surrounding and connecting the buildings.
  • On the western side are more practical buildings that hold Warder housing, kitchens, offices, etc. Surrounding these however are martial training grounds and fighting rings.
  • The whole thing is surrounded by a wall and located near the center of Haven, at the base of the corpse of Shun-Aush.

docs.title: Member Roles
docs.text:
• Magus: A general wizard who fills multiple roles
  • Arcanist: A wizard who focuses on research and experimentation. Primary keepers of the library.
  • Battle Magus: serves in the army and city guard
  • Archmage: Leader of the academy and member of the city council

docs.title: Warder roles
docs.text:
• Warder-Cadet: trainee
  • Hall-Warder: Guards the academy grounds
  • Shield-Warder: Guards wizards out in the field and serves alongside Battle Magi in the army/city guard
  • Warder-at-arms: Trainers, administration, assigns warders to wizards
  • High Warder: Top-level warders who reports to the Archmages

docs.title: Kreil Dirn
docs.text: Haven spymaster met the party in the Embered Horn, giving them a task to track down the Fanewraith and stop their plot to steal the Sowing Eye.
